content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper investigates a zero-shot HOI recognition task by exploring the pre-trained image caption models (GIT) and contrastive models (CLIP). The caption model (teacher) generates HOI-related captions, followed by pseudo-label distillation to obtain supervision, and finally the CLIP-initialized classifier predicts the HOI classification labels. The model achieves good performance on HICO, even on par with some strongly-supervised works.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
- The presentation of the paper is easy to follow.
- This work achieves a good performance on a zero-shot HOI recognition task.

Cons:
- I think the nature of this work is to distillate knowledge from multiple pretrained models, including an image captioning model (GIT), a CLIP classifier and a language model (SimCSE). There is no clear explanation why such a combination is good. 
- Why does the captioning model (GIT) just generate HOI-related captions? What about the generated captions that are not human-centric?
- The comparison with CLIP is not fair. As this work adopts more external knowledge (especially data) from pretrained models for HOI recognition. Would it be possible to use the same dataset to pre-train the image captioning model and CLIP classifier?
- Could the authors also provide some discussions about the generalization ability to other image classification tasks?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Novelty: I have some concern about the novelty on this paper. As I mentioned before, this paper is something like a combination of multiple pretrained models for HOI recognition. Although it achives considerate performance (also ablations), it is still unclear to me why such a design is specialized for HOI recognition rather than generalized image classification.
content.summary_of_the_review: I'm on the fence of accepting this paper. I think the experiment results are interesting and might benefit the HOI recognition commuty. However, I'm also concerned about the issues I listed above.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This work tackles a new zero-shot setup for the task of human object interaction, more focuses on the classification setting, where no HOI labels are available. To complete the task, the authors propose to leverage the strength of both generative model of image captioning (GIT) and image-text contrastive model (CLIP) along with the pretrained text similarity model to produce the supervisory signal to train the HOI model with the proposed pseudo-label distillation which extract HOI probabilities from image captions to train the student model. Finally, the proposed method achieves unprecedented 49.6 mAP on the HICO dataset without any ground-truth labels.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. The proposed method first tackles stricter zero-shot setting without requiring using any labels and show superior performance over other baseline methods.
2. The proposed method leverage pretrained image captioning model and the CLIP model to perform zero-shot HOI classification without requiring any HOI labeled dataset.

Weakness
1. The work still requires to know the possible action categories. When the action categories are open and there are action names with similar text but different meaning (which can not be handled well using WordNet as well), the proposed method may not be able to handle well.
2. Although the proposed method does not require any HOI label, it relies on very strong image captioning model and image-text contrastive model where both models are pretrained with very large-scale datasets.
3. When the proposed method is applied to a more difficult task, HOI-DET, there is still a huge performance gap with other methods, such as GEN-VLKT.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well-written and easy to follow. The paper also provides sufficient details to reproduce the results.
Although the proposed method relies on powerful pretrained models, since the work is the first to tackle the zero-shot HOI task without requiring any HOI labels, it is novel the proposed setup and method.
content.summary_of_the_review:
As shown in Table 4, when exploiting weaker image captioning, the performance drops significantly for some cases. The main success of achieving better performances than other supervised methods come from wisely employing powerful pretrained image caption and image-text contrastive models. In addition, the proposed method does have its merit for the task of novel zero-shot HOI task. The paper is well written with sufficient experimental results. 

When the authors generate the pseudo labels, do you do any special processing or directly convert the <verb, object> into a sentence with a fixed prompt template "some is verbing with object"? followed by computing the text similarities between the caption and the converted prompt?

I still have questions: since the outputs of the image caption model are unconstrained, when the generated caption does not work reasonably or contain the context for pseudo-label distillation, how does the proposed method handle or reject such samples?

In addition, the author could also comment if the proposed method can achieve better performance for HICO-DET when using better object detectors, such as YOLOv7 etc. or can be used to replace the HOI classification head of GEN-VLKT for better performance.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a method for Human Object Interaction learning that aims at training an image classifier based on CLIP from the captions generated by an image captioning model (GIT). A similarity score is computed between the captions and pairs of HOI classes to assign a list of manually defined pairs to each image. Using the generated pseudo-labels an image classifier is trained to produce the final outputs in a generalized scenario. The method is validated on several datasets delivering competitive results, and it is accompanied by several ablation studies.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The idea is interesting and has potential to generate interest. The use of a captioning model along with a vision-language discriminative model is a powerful way to enhance the latter to produce better models for zero-shot classification. 

However, the paper is not very well presented in my opinion, and many important details are missing or concealed within the text. After several reads there are many aspects of the paper that are not clear to me:

- In Section 5.2: For the teacher network i.e. the GIT, it is said that “We generate pseudo-labels on the training set, and use a threshold of 0.97 to convert them to binary labels”. This statement requires further explanation. I wonder what the pseudo-labels refer to in this sentence, the captions or the classes that maximize Eqn. 4. How are these converted into binary labels and how are these used thereafter?

- In Section 4.1: “The teacher achieves 35.6 mAP on HICO when we convert the captioning output to class logits by evaluating text similarities. The student model achieves 25.8 mAP (the zero-shot performance of CLIP ViT-B/32).” The student model is supposed to be a classifier producing logits. My understanding is that the authors perform the zero-shot classification using the standard prompt-based approach, but this is not specified. Similarly, details are missing for the teacher model. 

- In Section 4.2: “ti denotes a sentence converted from the i th HOI class (e.g., is converted to “a person riding a bicycle”).” How is this process done? Is it manual, is it defined for all classes? This needs further explanation. 

- In Section 4.2: “π(oi , oτ ) represents the WordNet-based mask between the object in the i th HOI class and the object in caption τ .” How is the object computed from the caption? This is very important because it makes me wonder why the whole caption to label matching is needed if the object can be retrieved automatically from the caption! Why working on the BERT-based embedding space when the objects can be inferred directly from the caption?

- I miss an overall learning procedure or algorithm in the paper or supplementary material. It is not really clear what is being trained and not and how many iterations are needed to update the classifier. 

- It seems to me that the pseudo-labelling occurs only once at the beginning of the training using the GIT captions, as such model does not seem to be updated at all during the training. Is this the case? My understanding is that the pseudo-captions are generated at the beginning of the training and never used again in the teacher-student process. Once the captions and pseudo-labels are generated the classifier based on CLIP is learned using the generated classes. Indeed, it is barely mentioned in Section 7 an attempt to fine-tune the GIT model as well. I believe the paper would strengthen significantly by developing such Section further. 

- It is not very clear, or I missed that part, how the labels are assigned to an image to train the teacher. The paper describes the computation of the class probabilities but it is not specified how the classes are chosen. There is a sparsification process to generate a smaller list of pseudo-labels but it is not clear to me how the list is used. Indeed, From Figure 2 I can see that the likelihood of the ground-truth class to be Top-1 doesn’t seem to be significant, which might be detrimental to the performance of the method.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is novel to some extend, but it is hard to depict the extend to which this is the case considering the quality of the presentation. Many details are missing making reproducibility hard.
content.summary_of_the_review: In my opinion, the paper shows an interesting idea worth working on, but is a bit limited in the sense that the teacher network is not updated and the fact that the training is solely based on these initial pseudolabels. The poor presentation and clarity also prevents me from recommending this paper at this point for acceptance.

content.title: Zero-shot Human-Object Interaction Recognition by Bridging Generative and Contrastive Image-Language Models
content.TL;DR: Our zero-shot HOI classifier outperforms supervised SOTAs by using a heterogeneous teach-student framework which bridges generative and contrastive pre-trained image-language models through pseudo-label distillation.
content.abstract: Existing studies in Human-Object Interaction (HOI) recognition rely heavily on costly human-annotated labels, limiting the application of HOI in real-world scenarios like retail and surveillance. To address this issue, this paper investigates a new zero-shot setup where no HOI labels are available for any image. We propose a novel heterogenous teacher-student framework that bridges two types of pre-trained models, namely contrastive (e.g., CLIP) and generative (e.g., GIT) image-language models. To bridge their gap, we introduce pseudo-label distillation to extract HOI probabilities from image captions to train the student classifier. Our method leverages the complementary strengths of both models. As a result, the student model has "the best of two worlds", e.g., the compact backbone of a contrastive model and the fine-grained discriminability of a generative (captioning) model. It achieves 49.6 mAP on the HICO dataset without any ground-truth labels, becoming a new state-of-the-art that outperforms previous supervised approaches. Code will be released upon acceptance.
